drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (not quantified in data but implied by ACWR spike and zone distribution shift), ACWR likely elevated — this month’s 5 runs at 23.8 km with 37% Z4 effort contrasts sharply with last month’s 10 runs at 51.3 km with only 8% Z4; aerobic TE increased from 2.6 to 3.0, indicating reduced fatigue resistance; resting HR not provided but avg HR rose from 134 to 144 bpm despite slower average pace (534 → 523 sec/km), suggesting autonomic strain; cadence dropped from 149 to 134 spm, consistent with neuromuscular fatigue
readiness.guidance: This week must prioritize restoration — no intensity, minimal volume, and emphasis on sleep hygiene and HRV-supportive habits.

monthly_review.summary: Volume and intensity have contracted sharply this month versus last, with a marked shift toward higher-zone work and declining efficiency metrics — suggesting either intentional taper or emerging fatigue.
monthly_review.highlight: The 10-bpm rise in average heart rate despite faster average pace — coupled with a 15-spm cadence drop and elevated aerobic TE — signals disproportionate physiological stress, not improved fitness.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km would require 27.5 km across 5 remaining sessions — an average of 5.5 km/session — but recovery status is compromised, making volume chasing unsafe and counterproductive; priority must shift from distance targets to restoring autonomic resilience.

insights.title: Elevated HR without pace improvement suggests sympathetic dominance
insights.body: Avg HR rose +10 bpm (134 → 144) while pace improved only marginally (+11 sec/km), and cadence fell -15 spm — classic signs of compensatory effort under reduced parasympathetic tone, not performance gain.

insights.title: Z4 dominance replaced Z1 foundation — undermining aerobic base
insights.body: Z1 time collapsed from 43% (Aug) to 10% (Sep), while Z4 surged from 8% to 37%; this abrupt shift contradicts periodisation logic and coincides with rising aerobic TE (2.6 → 3.0) and falling efficiency (14.12 → 14.18).

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off indicates compromised neuromuscular coordination
insights.body: Cadence dropped from 149 spm (Aug) to 134 spm (Sep), yet stride length increased (e.g., 94.09 cm on 2026-08-27 vs 77.22 cm on 2026-09-06) — suggesting overstriding compensation, especially during the 10.7 km run where ground contact rose to 327 ms and cadence fell to 90 spm.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤128 bpm, 4.0 km, Tuesday — focus on cadence ≥145 spm using metronome
recommendations.reason: Restores aerobic stimulus without cardiac or neural load; counters recent cadence collapse and autonomic strain

recommendations.action: Complete 3x 10-min guided HRV biofeedback sessions (morning, pre-coffee), using breath pacing at 5.5 s/inhale–5.5 s/exhale
recommendations.reason: Directly targets parasympathetic re-engagement; required before any Z3+ reintroduction

recommendations.action: Sleep extension protocol: bedtime moved 30 min earlier for next 7 nights; no screens after 20:30; track sleep duration — target ≥7.5 hr/night
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is unmeasured but inferred from HRV suppression, rising HR, and efficiency decline; foundational for recovery balance restoration

risk_flags.evidence: ACWR spike inferred from 37% Z4 effort in low-volume month (vs 8% Z4 in higher-volume August); aerobic TE ↑0.4%, avg HR ↑10 bpm, cadence ↓15 spm, efficiency ↓0.06 ml/kg/km
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z3+ work until aerobic TE ≤2.5 and cadence stabilises ≥142 spm for 3 consecutive easy runs

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish parasympathetic tone through low-intensity movement, structured breathing, and sleep discipline — prioritising nervous system recovery over mechanical or metabolic output.
suggested_sessions: Walking or mobility session with heart rate monitoring (keep <110 bpm)
